description: The Nature-based Solutions Evidence Tool is an interactive map from the Nature-based Solutions Initiative at the University of Oxford that links nature-based solutions to climate change adaptation outcomes, based on a systematic review of the peer-reviewed literature. Users can explore the evidence on nature-based interventions, compare their social, economic and ecological effects, filter by criteria, generate maps and graphs, and connect the findings to national climate policy; a separate view covers scenario modelling evidence. The tool is free to use online and is embedded on the Initiative's website; no licence is stated for the underlying evidence database. Caveats: the map is rendered by scripts and the underlying review data is not offered as a download on the page read, and the evidence reflects the published studies included in the review. Coverage is worldwide, by country. It supports climate adaptation planning with green and blue infrastructure, such as choosing interventions for flood, heat or coastal protection; related records are the Urban Nature Atlas, Oppla and the NetworkNature knowledge databases.
